title: Parsing one aligned bit pair
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x=\mathrm{pre}\,b\,d\,\mathrm{rest}$ for Boolean words $\mathrm{pre},\mathrm{rest}$ and bits $b,d$, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$, and let $\mathrm{out}$ be a Boolean word. Starting in the threaded-map parser with its pair-reading state set by an emitting flag $e$, input head at position $|\mathrm{pre}|+1$, capture head at displacement $0$, and output $\mathrm{out}$, after two steps the input head is at position $|\mathrm{pre}|+3$ and the output is $\mathrm{out}$ followed by $[b,d]$ if $e$ is true, and is otherwise unchanged. The resulting state continues pair parsing if $b=d$, halts if $b=1,d=0$, and enters the post-separator phase if $b=0,d=1$.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite Boolean Turing machine
x equals pre followed by bits b,d and rest
pre and rest are Boolean words
c is an M-configuration on x
e is a Boolean emitting flag
replaced:
If the input splits as $x = p\, b\, d\, s$ with bits $b, d$, two steps of the
threaded-map controller from its block-start parse state at position
$\abs{p}$ continue parsing when $b = d$, halt when $(b,d) = (1,0)$, and pass
to the post-separator state when $(b,d) = (0,1)$; both bits are emitted
exactly when the controller is in its emitting pass. The captured word and
its head are preserved.
